issue.description:
Result: Independently accept or return the complete continuation plan and every expanded task before any proposed task or dependency is written.

Starting condition: The implementation and prior accepted work already exist. This draft recovers unfinished delivery after the earlier cloud sessions disappeared; it does not recreate the earlier 37 tasks. The previous complete review found one blocking command error, now corrected, and must not be presented as acceptance of this reconstructed version.

Locations and inputs: /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/coordination/plan.json and /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/coordination/manifest.json; the original user request; /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/references/workflow.md, planner.md, execution.md, zcf.md and language.md. Read both product handoffs at /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/worktrees/bead-completion/.marathon/progress.md and /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/worktrees/scotty-completion/docs/backend-compatibility.md, and /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/coordination/original-plan-review.json.

Prerequisites: The reviewed continuation plan has been accepted before this task is stored or assigned.

Required behavior: Native editing covers title, description, priority with a reason, issue type, notes, status and assignee, plus the existing label and dependency actions. Keep ID, timestamps, claims, recorded history and unrelated records intact. Use the accepted issue-editing-v1 contract in /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/worktrees/bead-completion/research/specs/issue-editing-v1.md. Windows production launchers must have one tray icon with Exit and stop only their own server processes.

Steps:
1. Read the entire exact plan and every expanded description. Compare all requested fields, dependency editing, tray Exit, installed use, preservation, parallel work, Git publication, task records and cleanup against the user request and accepted contract.
2. Trace every required result to task keys and actual blocking edges. Verify that independent cloud work can proceed while PC work is serialized, and static review can start before execution completes.
3. Check every instruction for concrete inputs, commands or input-acquisition steps, pass/fail criteria, return records and Git completion. Check the whole text against the current language exclusions. Confirm old failures remain visible and passing prior work is not unnecessarily repeated.
4. Verify R1 from original-plan-review.json: cloud-checks no longer invokes the real priority browser flow as a standalone node test; browser-check retains that coverage through the native-ui integration runner. Check changed storage/build/session conditions and unavailable old logs.
5. Return pass, fail or pending with concrete corrections and exact SHA-256 hashes of both reviewed files. On a correction, review the complete revised plan again. Root may materialize only the accepted revision, then record this passed review in the resulting task.

Required checks and completion: Pass requires a complete, independently executable, acyclic graph with all user results covered and a route through actual Windows installation and final cleanup. Do not accept sampled task descriptions. No test execution or task-store write is allowed in this review.

Permissions and limits: Work in the cloud where possible. Root alone uses Emergency Maintenance on the PC and writes canonical task state. Keep the PC free for the user's Unreal/VR work: no PC builds, GPU use, visible browser or other UI control, service restarts, broad process termination, or changes to unrelated projects. Ordinary PC app runs are sequential, hidden, BelowNormal, with a 256 MiB Node heap and a 512 MiB total owned-process resident-memory cap. Read free RAM first and require at least 3 GiB before starting an app run; stop this task's processes if their memory cap is exceeded or foreground work shows resource pressure. The small helper diagnostic has its stricter 200 MiB total cap and 90-second maximum. Browser checks belong in the cloud. Preserve the existing PC native checkpoint and all Scotty machine-local task data. Do not initialize, replace, or upload the Scotty task store. Protect other workers' files. Reviewers inspect files and supplied results; they do not execute product tests or builds. On a new failed check, retain the exact error and stop the affected acceptance; send the concrete defect to root for a reviewed repair. Never repeat a mutation after a timeout until its result is reconciled. Do not obtain another process's claim credential.

Return /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/coordination/results/plan-review.json with status, source_commits, binary_sha256 when relevant, checks and their exits, output_paths, changed_files, open_items, and git_result. State which requirement each check established and its limits. Mark lost earlier cloud output as unavailable; do not cite a deleted log as retained. Later work may proceed only after its listed prerequisites pass; a candidate record alone is not acceptance.

Git completion: Commit only this task's authorized repository changes. Before the checked installation, push backend changes to YossiMH/bead-rs task/bead-finish-20261124 and app changes to YossiMH/bead-me-up-scotty task/scotty-finish-20261124, keeping main at the installer's verified baseline. The recovered app working branch is task/scotty-recovered-20261124; use ordinary descendant publication to its named remote task branch. After installation, publish completed changes to main by ordinary fast-forward integration. Never force-push or include private local task data. Report the commit and verified remote ref. With no changes, check for this task's unpublished commits and otherwise report no changes; do not create an empty commit. If pushing fails, try another independently permitted Git route, record the failure and next permitted retry, and continue useful authorized work. A failed push alone does not prevent task closure or the next task.

issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted 2026-08-12) decides to add a third dependency kind `verifies` so authors can declare check relationships, and to diagnose inverted verification gates structurally (a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its blocked bead) — reported advisories, never rejected at insert, never inferred from titles. No open bead covers R025. Work: extend the dependency model and CLI (e.g. `bead dep add --kind verifies`), add the structural inversion diagnosis to doctor/dependency reporting, keep cycle validation accepting inverted edges (a two-node ring can be both), and record the new kind in the field guide / `bead schema explain` output plus research/specs. Tests: inversion is advisory only and never affects eligibility; cycle+inversion interaction; round-trip of the new edge kind through the checkpoint including the unknown-field corpus; a negative test proving no code path consults issue titles. Caution: untracked tests/dependency_blocker_status.rs is in the tree — confirm it is not already in-flight coverage before starting.
